A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with the same authors, framework, and central consistency theorem. All pages are readable, including v4's Appendix 8. V3 contains its proofs in the main text and has no separate appendix.

before.justification: V3 presents mathematical results and constructed examples, but no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes. Empirical findings are attributed to cited research.

after.justification: V4 remains theoretical, including its appendix. The added proposition, proof, and transducer definitions do not constitute empirical results.

M1.justification: The tokenizer remains a pair of stochastic encoder and decoder maps. V4 revises mathematical characterizations of tokenizers without introducing or changing an implemented tokenization algorithm, training procedure, or inference method.

E1.justification: Neither version trains or evaluates on datasets or tasks. Added discussion of linguistic segmentation and character-level language models does not introduce evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated baselines. BPE, WordPiece, and Unigram remain examples in theoretical discussion, rather than participants in experimental comparisons.

E3.justification: Neither version specifies an empirical evaluation protocol. V4's new string-distance definition supports its mathematical analysis; it is not an evaluation metric used in an experiment.

E4.justification: No ablations, robustness tests, or empirical supplementary analyses are introduced. V3's ambiguity and uncomputability examples are retained as Examples 8.1 and 8.2 in v4, rather than added analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or empirical uncertainty estimates. Discussion of estimator consistency is theoretical.

E6.justification: Figure 1 retains the same illustrative distributions: (0.2, 0.4, 0.4), encoded as (0.2, 0, 0.8) and decoded as (0, 0.2, 0.8). No experimental result entries are added or revised; the new mathematical result is assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Section 5 replaces finite-type maps and bounded tokenizers in Definitions 5.3–5.4 with a prefix-based string distance and bounded variation. V4 adds Proposition 5.2, proving that multiplicativity implies bounded variation, invokes Choffrut's subsequentiality criterion, and adds sequential/subsequential transducer definitions in Appendix 8.3. This substantially revises the computational theory. The central consistency theorem and its existing supporting proofs are retained and relocated.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the unified stochastic-map framework and necessary-and-sufficient consistency guarantee. The supporting computational contribution changes from tractability and boundedness through finite decomposition to finiteness and sequentiality through bounded variation.

C2.justification: V4 qualifies the cited practical impact of spurious ambiguity as occurring mostly on strongly out-of-domain evaluation sets and adds a linguistic-segmentation prerequisite for modeling linguistic ambiguity. It also removes v3's explicit limitations concerning structural questions, vocabulary choice, effective computation, interpretability, and potential empirical investigation. These alter qualifications while retaining the central interpretations of inconsistency and ambiguity.

D1.justification: No implementation recipe, experimental hyperparameters, hardware information, or work-specific code/data access is added or removed. The new appendix definitions are mathematical specifications, not reproducibility information for an implementation.

R1.justification: V4 adds connections to Berstel and Choffrut's transduction theory, Lehmann and Casella's estimation text, linguistic-tokenization studies, and work by Giulianelli et al. and Vieira et al. These broaden the supporting literature and connect the framework to follow-up character-level modeling while retaining its overall foundational positioning.

P1.justification: The main exposition is substantially reorganized: existing proofs move to Appendix 8.1 and two worked examples to Appendix 8.2. Section 5 is rewritten around sequentiality, preliminary explanations and terminology are revised, and the limitations section is removed. These changes materially alter the narrative structure despite preserving much of the underlying content.

P2.justification: V4 introduces systematic green/violet mathematical notation, reformats Figure 1 from a vertically stacked display into a side-by-side arrangement, and adds an identity arrow to the main commutative diagram. The overall single-column format remains, with no new experimental tables or plots.

improvement.justification: V4 develops Section 5 more fully through bounded variation, the proved Proposition 5.2, and explicit transducer definitions. Collecting existing proofs and examples in the appendix also streamlines the main argument without removing their support. These provide a modest gain in theoretical development and readability, although deleting v3's limitations section weakens transparency about unresolved questions and constrains the overall improvement.
